# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 1B.10 evidence note

Bottom line: **slightly safer than inherited, but only modestly so**. The strongest 2024 evidence points to improved macro stability, a more formalized nuclear-safety / arms-control posture, and repeated de-escalatory messaging. The main offsetting evidence is rights-constrained politics and some sharp Kashmir/India rhetoric that kept the crisis environment tense.

| Valence | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan’s nuclear-security regime page | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Updated in May 2024; standing page | https://mofa.gov.pk/vienna-pakistans-nuclear-safety-seccurity-regime | Pakistan said it updated its nuclear-security regime booklet in May 2024, renewed practical arrangements with the IAEA, and maintained formal oversight through the NCA/SPD structure. That is the clearest evidence of improved institutional safety posture during Sharif’s term. | 1B.10; also 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Standing policy page; current version cites a May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s policy page says it supports CTBT objectives, a unilateral testing moratorium, FMCT negotiations, IAEA safeguards, reciprocal inspections proposals, UNSCR 1540 implementation, export controls, and multilateral nonproliferation norms. That suggests a more disciplined posture than a posture of open risk-taking. | 1B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and nuclear safety/security architecture. This supports a more transparent and institution-facing risk posture. | 1B.10; also 1B.4, 1B.7, 1B.9 |
| Favorable | PM urges India to engage in dialogue for resolution of J&K dispute | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | Sharif urged India to enter dialogue for a peaceful Kashmir resolution at UNGA. This is direct de-escalatory evidence and supports a safer crisis posture. | 1B.10; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | PM voices satisfaction over Pakistan Army’s operational preparedness | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/05-09-2024/pm-expresses-satisfaction-over-pak-armys-operational-preparedness | Sharif framed preparedness as preserving the balance of power for peace in nuclearized South Asia and limiting costs to the event of aggression. This reads as deterrence-and-stability management, not reckless escalation. | 1B.10; also 1B.5, 1B.8 |
| Mixed | Pakistan’s election-day telecom and mobile internet shutdown is a reckless attack on people’s rights | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/ | Amnesty condemned the election-day shutdown as a rights violation. That does not speak directly to nuclear posture, but it indicates a coercive political environment around Sharif’s ascent and weighs against a clean “safer” judgment overall. | 1B.10; also 1B.2, 1B.8 |
| Mixed | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | The same UNGA speech also used hard-edged rhetoric about India’s military expansion and a “limited war under the nuclear overhanging.” That is not a direct threat, but it kept the crisis temperature elevated. | 1B.10; also 1B.2, 1B.5, 1B.8 |
| Favorable | Pakistan’s nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif said Pakistan’s nuclear program is peaceful, defensive, and non-aggressive. This is the clearest late-2024 stewardship statement and supports a safer end-state than a more openly dangerous one. | 1B.10; also 1B.1, 1B.2, 1B.5 |

## Search gap

- I did **not** find direct 2024 evidence of a major war scare that Sharif clearly defused through private crisis channels.
- I also did **not** find direct evidence of a catastrophic escalation, proliferation episode, or nuclear-safety failure under his watch.
- So the “safer vs. more dangerous” judgment is necessarily inferential: the year looks **modestly safer** because formal safety institutions and de-escalatory diplomacy improved, but the improvement is limited by political coercion and persistent brinkmanship.
